comments.author: @sebastianotumminello9150
comments.text:
Watching the video, you get the gist: Italians live in paradise, but their standard of living is hellish. Does the author know Italy? Have you lived in Italy to judge? You talk about high rents without realizing that 85% of Italians own their own homes. Those who rent are almost all non-EU citizens. And don't worry...they pay €100 a month for public housing. Can you imagine and see all this misery in Italy? We're the fifth richest country in the world, second or third (we're alternating with France) richest in Europe. The GDP of the Lombardy region is higher than the entire nation of Austria or Belgium.
And all the young people are running away? What movies do you watch?
You should know that it's not how much you earn that matters, but how much life costs...region by region. Consider the numbers for Milan...just live in a nearby city and those numbers are halved. Go to Sicily, and rent in a small town can cost you €150-200 a month. You earn less, and everything costs less.
Every weekend, millions of Italians eat out, go to museums, shop, and take nature trips, and you talk about a hell in heaven?
Look at the numbers on how many Italians take summer vacations, whether in the mountains or on the beach. Look at the numbers for Christmas and New Year's holidays, and whether hotels or restaurants are available for reservations.
But yes...you think we live in despair. Truly travel around Italy and see how sad we all are, with empty cities.
We're doing very well,
and it shouldn't be a foreigner who knows little about Italy who makes false judgments.

replies.author: @sebastianotumminello9150
replies.text:
​​​@HiddenTravel-g9hLet's analyze things from afar.
About 30 million Italians have emigrated abroad over the last 140 years. 
The descendants of these emigrants now number around 80 million.
Can you imagine a modern-day Italy with 140 million inhabitants?
Thank God they left, or we were like sardines in a can.
Now let's move on to young people.
In the last 15 years, 650,000 have left Italy, and around 200,000 have returned.
In the same period, around 900,000 young non-EU citizens entered Italy.
How can we provide a living for these people if Italians flee abroad?
Italy was built by farmers and workers in the post-war period.
People without education but with a desire to work.
And for decades we enjoyed the famous economic miracle with skyrocketing annual GDP.
Look carefully and do research on Italy's need for specialized labor.
We need over a million technicians in various industrial sectors, including healthcare, tech startups, and the energy transition.
Then, over a million specialized industrial machine operators.
The truth is, today's young people want everything, and possibly without breaking a sweat.
Their grandfathers and fathers built Italy's prosperity by working hard.
They want prosperity in a suit and tie.
I understand, and we need to improve, but if everyone wears their Sunday best...
who builds the roads, the houses, or grows and processes the food we eat?
Bottom line...let them go abroad if they want to improve.
Two rabbits in a field live well.
A hundred can survive, but a thousand cause famine and disease.
I was born when Italy had 45 million inhabitants and things were better than today.
Let them go abroad; a little more space creates fresh air.

replies.text: Italy clearly has a great quality of life in many places, but that doesn't erase the economic issues. The OECD reports that real wages were still 7.5% below early-2021 levels in 2025, and over 400,000 young Italians left the country between 2012 and 2023.
